register.description: Function code, Run control/status, Stall Result control.

bitfield.description: Set to zero on Write, ignore on Read

When written with a1b updating of the PKA_COMPARE, PKA_MSW and PKA_DIVMSW registers, as well as resetting the Run bit is stalled beyond the point that a running operation is actually finished. Use this to allow software enough time to read results from a previous operation when the newly started operation is known to take only a short amount of time. If a result is waiting, the result registers is updated and the Run bit is reset in the clock cycle following Writing the Stall Result bit back to0b The Stall result function may only be used for basic PKCP operations
Set to zero on Write, ignore on Read.
These bits are an extend of bits [14:12] to select the complex Sequencer operation to perform

The host sets this bit to instruct the PKA module to begin processing the basic PKCP or complex Sequencer operation. This bit is reset low automatically when the operation is complete. The complement of this bit is available as interrupt see sections 5.6.5 and 5.6.6. After a reset, the Run bit is always set to1b Depending on the configuration, Program ROM or Program RAM, the following applies: Program ROM The first Sequencer instruction sets the bit to0b This is done immediately after the hardware reset is released. Program RAM The Sequencer needs to set the bit to0b As a valid firmware may not have been loaded, the Sequencer is held in software reset after the hardware reset is released [the Reset bit in PKA_SEQ_CRTL is set to1b. After the FW image is loaded and the Reset bit is cleared, the Sequencer starts to execute the FW. The first instruction clears the Run bit. In both cases a few clock cycles are needed before the first instruction is executed and the Run bit state has been propagated
These bits in combination with bits [18:16] select the complex Sequencer operation to perform

register.description: PE bypass and dual LNME linking control.

bitfield.description: Bits should be written with 0 and should be ignored on a read.

This bit controls the 'linking ' of the two LNME PE chains in a dual LNME [if configured, otherwise this field must be treated as 'Reserved ']. When set to1b all PEs of the 2nd chain are inserted at the end of the 1st chain [in front of the 'terminating PE '], the X-FIFOs are combined into one and the LNME FIFO memories are combined to form a dual depth FIFO.Note: This bit cannot be changed while an operation is busy in either the 1st or the 2nd LNME.
Bits should be written with 0 and should be ignored on a read.
This field controls the PE chain bypass multiplexers for the 2nd LNME. The number of bits is 3 for 12-PE configurations.Note: This field cannot be changed while an operation is busy in the 2nd LNME.
Bits should be written with 0 and should be ignored on a read.
This field controls the PE chain bypass multiplexers for the 1st LNME. The number of bits is 3 for 12-PE configurations.Note: This field cannot be changed while an operation is busy in the 1st LNME.

Write-only, bit should be written with1bwhen updating bits [30:16], always reads0b When Writing this bit with a0b bits [30:16] will not be changed irrespective the values written there. Updating bits [30:16] can only be done with a single write action, separate Byte writes are not possible.

This field controls the value XOR-ed into the vector index fields of the LNME_FAST_MMM and LNME_FAST_STRT registers when the xor_ctrl is1bupon starting an MMM3A and/or PKCP ADDSUB operation using those registers. The actual XOR is only done when a vector index field equals the cmp_value field in the bits that are1bin the cmp_mask field. To modify this field, the update bit should be written with a1b

This field contains bits that are compared against the vector index fields of the LNME_FAST_MMM and LNME_FAST_STRT registers when starting an MMM3A and/or PKCP ADDSUB operation using those registers. Comparison is only done for the corresponding1bbits in the cmp_mask field, other bits are don 't care. To modify this field, the update bit should be written with a 1b

This field controls which bits of the vector index fields of the LNME_FAST_MMM and LNME_FAST_STRT registers are compared against cmp_value when starting an MMM3A and/or PKCP ADDSUB operation using those registers. A1bin this field compares the corresponding bit in the cmp_value field; a0bin this field makes the corresponding cmp_value bit a don 't care. To modify this field, the update bit should be written with a1b
These bits are ignored on a write and will read zero on a read. These bits are intended to allow Writing any value to bits [15:1] while setting the xor_ctrl bit

This bit controls whether or not the value in the xor_mask field is XOR-ed into the vector index fields of the LNME_FAST_MMM and LNME_FAST_STRT registers. The state of this bit is logged with an MMM3A or ADDSUB operation request using those registers and may be changed immediately after that point.

This bit controls which operation is actually performed in the PKCP:A0brequests an ADD operation, which is performed using the ADDSUB A+C-B operation, with the A and C vectors controlled by the addsub_a and addsub_bc fields here. The B vector of the PKCP should point to a suitable vector containing the value zero. As both the input vectors can be up to 2 times the Modulus in value, the result can be close to 4 times the Modulus vector value.A1brequests a SUB operation, which is performed using the ADDSUB A+C-B operation, with the A and B vectors controlled by the addsub_a and addsub_bc fields here. The C vector of the PKCP should point to a suitable vector containing 2 times the Modulus value. As both the input vectors can be up to 2 times the Modulus in value, the result can be close to 4 times the Modulus vector value [in case A is at its maximum value and B equals zero].
This holds the index for the PKCP ADDSUB result vector 'D ' in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register].
This holds the index for the PKCP ADDSUB operation 'B ' or 'C ' input vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register].
This holds the index for the PKCP ADDSUB operation 'A ' input vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register].
Bits should be written with 0 and should be ignored on a read.

This bit will be set to1bwhen an MMM3A operation is requested in the 2nd LNME by Writing to bits [31:16] of the LNME_FAST_MMM register with a non-zero value. The operation is started as soon as possible, i.e. when both LNMEs and the PKCP are ready for a next operation - if an operation was already busy in the 2nd LNME, the LNME1 interrupt may only activate for a single clock cycle. This bit automatically falls back to0bwhen the operation is actually started, at which point both the mmm and mmm_next bits in the LNME1_CTRL register are set to1b To abort this request, write this bit with a1b- Writing a0bhas no effect.Note: This bit is 'Reserved ' in a normal [non-dual] LNME configuration.

This bit will be set to1bwhen an MMM3A operation is requested in the 1st LNME by Writing to bits [15:0] of the LNME_FAST_MMM register with a non-zero value. The operation is started as soon as possible, i.e. when both LNMEs and the PKCP are ready for a next operation - if an operation was already busy in the 1st LNME, the LNME0 interrupt may only activate for a single clock cycle. This bit automatically falls back to0bwhen the operation is actually started, at which point both the mmm and mmm_next bits in the LNME0_CTRL register are set to1b To abort this request, write this bit with a1b- Writing a0bhas no effect.

This bit will be set to1bwhen an ADDSUB operation is requested in the PKCP by Writing to bits [31:16] of this register with a non-zero value. The operation is started as soon as possible, i.e. when both LNMEs and the PKCP are ready for a next operation. This bit automatically falls back to0bwhen the operation is actually started. To abort this request, write this bit with a1b- Writing a0bhas no effect.

Bit should be written with1bto request updating the sticky_oflo and sticky_zero status bits in the LNME1_STATUS register. When this bit is written0b those status bits are not modified at the end of the MMM3A operation. Note: This field is 'Reserved ' in a normal [non-dual] LNME configuration.

This holds the index for the 2nd LNME 's result vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register]. Note: This field is 'Reserved ' in a normal [non-dual] LNME configuration.

This holds the index for the 2nd LNME 's Y input vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register]. Note: This field is 'Reserved ' in a normal [non-dual] LNME configuration.

This holds the index for the 2nd LNME 's X input vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register]. Note: This field is 'Reserved ' in a normal [non-dual] LNME configuration.

Bit should be written with1bto request updating the sticky_oflo and sticky_zero status bits in the LNME0_STATUS register. When this bit is written0b those status bits are not modified at the end of the MMM3A operation.
This holds the index for the 1st LNME 's result vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register].
This holds the index for the 1st LNME 's Y input vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register].
This holds the index for the 1st LNME 's X input vector in the table [before possible XOR-ing with the xor_value field in the LNME_FAST_CTRL register].

Command opcode:000bClear tgt operand register.001bCopy src0 operand to tgt operand register.010bGF[2m] Add src0 and src1 operands, write result to tgt operand.011bGF[2m] Multilpy src0 and src1 operands, write result to tgt operand.100bShift-xor-loop operation to assist a GF[2m] Inverse operation. All other opcode combinations are reserved and should not be used. Refer to Table 19 for more detailed command information.

Setting this bit [cmd_submit] submits the command that is specified by the remaining bits in this register. The cmd_submit bit is self clearing. Writing this bit with0bhas no effect. Submitting a command always sets the busy bit in GF2M_STAT. In case a second command is submitted while the engine is still busy processing, the command will be buffered internally. The cmd_buf_full bit - that is returned when Reading this bit location - will be set to indicate that command buffer is fully occupied. The cmd_buf_full bit reads0bwhen the GF2m Engine is ready to accept a new command. When this bit reads1b the command buffer is full and no new command may be written.
This status bit reads1bwhen the GF2m Engine is processing a command. The irq output is the inverted level of this bit.
These bits should be written with zeroes and ignored on a read.

Represents the number of src0 operand right-shifts that was performed during the last 'shift-xor-loop ' operation. Note: In case the shift-xor-loop command did not find src0 bit [0] to become 'odd ' after [mul_rounds*mul_depth] cycles the shift_value reports 0x3ff, meaning 'invalid '.

Command error. Set to1bby hardware when trying to start a processing using a non-valid opcode. This bit is automatically cleared to0bby hardware on a start of any [legal] operation. The command error is also triggered when the shift-xor-loop command is executed with equal pointers in the src0 and src1 fields. Note: When the first command in a sequence of two commands [buffered commands] produces an error, the cmd_err bit remains active until the engine has finished processing, regardless if the second command was valid.
These bits should be written with zeroes and ignored on a read.
Result of the 'degree ' operation: If the last read operand word contains only zeroes, there is no MSB present in this word. In that case this bit will be1b
Result of the 'degree ' operation: Represents the index location of the MSB within the 32-bit operand word that was last read via the TCM interface.
These bits should be written with zeroes and ignored on a read.

This field must be populated with the 'operand shift ' value for the GF[2m] multiplication operation. The operand shift value is the offset from the MSB with respect to the left-shift boundaries. The operand shift value can be determined using the following expression: operand_shift = field size%mul_depth. Examples for commonly used field sizes and a multiplier depth [mul_depth] value of4:163-bit: 2 'b11, 233-bit: 2 'b01, 283-bit: 2 'b11, 409-bit: 2 'b01, 571-bit: 2 'b11
These bits should be written with zeroes and ignored on a read.

This field must be populated with the number of multiplier rounds for the GF[2m] operation. The number of multiplier rounds depends on the multiplier depth and the field size:mul_rounds = [field size/mul_depth]+1. The minimum value for this register is 0x1 and the maximum value 0x8F. Examples for commonly used field sizes and a multiplier depth [mul_depth] value of4:163-bit: 0x29, 233-bit: 0x3B, 283-bit: 0x47,409-bit: 0x67, 571-bit: 0x8F
These bits should be written with zeroes and ignored on a read.

Operand size. Represents the width of the operand registers inside the GF2m Engine. Value 0x23c means that the operand registers are 572 bits wide. The operand registers are one bit wider than the maximum supported filed size.
These bits should be written with zeroes and ignored on a read.
Multiplier matrix depth. Represents the number of AND-XOR matrix rows implemented in the GF2m Engine. Value 0x4 means that multiplier matrix contains four levels of AND-XOR matrix rows.
Number of implemented operand registers. Value 0x4 means four operands [A up to D].
These bits should be written with zeroes and ignored on a read.

Selects the module Idle mode. These bit combinations are only available: 00 = Force Idle mode: An IdleRequest is immediately acknowledged., 01 = No Idle mode: An IdleRequest is never acknowledged., 10 = Smart Idle mode: An IdleRequest is not acknowledged until the module is done processing [reset default]., 11 = Reserved

Raw GF2m Engine ready interrupt status. Note: The reset value of this bit is0b but this bit becomes1bdirectly after reset.
Raw combined LNME0 & LNME1 ready interrupt status. Note: The reset value of this bit is0b but this bit becomes1bdirectly after reset.

Raw main PKA interrupt status. The reset value of this bit is zero, but it will become high after a few cycles, to indicate that the PKA is ready to be used. For the Program ROM configuration this is within a few cycles after a reset, for the Program RAM configuration a few cycles after pulling the Sequencer out of reset [section 8.3.2], provided the firmware is loaded in Program RAM prior to that.
These bits should not be written and ignored on reads.

Masked GF2m Engine ready interrupt status.This interrupt can be enbled when setting the GF2mIrqEn bit in the PKA_IRQENABLE register. This interrupt can be cleared by Writing this bit. Writing1bclears the GF2m Engine ready interrupt.This bit is self-clearing; it does not have to be set to0bafterwards. Writing0bhas no effect.

Masked combined LNME0 & LNME1 ready interrupt status.This interrupt can be enbled when setting the LNMEIrqEn bit in the PKA_IRQENABLE register. This interrupt can be cleared by Writing this bit. Writing1bclears the combined LNME0 & LNME1 ready interrupt. This bit is self-clearing; it does not have to be set to0bafterwards. Writing0bhas no effect.

Masked main PKA interrupt status.This interrupt can be enbled when setting the PkaIrqEn bit in the PKA_IRQENABLE register. This interrupt can be cleared by Writing this bit. Writing1bclears the main PKA interrupt. This bit is self-clearing; it does not have to be set to0bafterwards. Writing0bhas no effect.
These bits should not be written and ignored on reads.
